title: fix(plugin-detail): memoise the record-grained write verdict per principal (objectui#10107)
body:
Part of #10107. Deliberately not a closing keyword: this repairs the half that lives in `packages/plugin-detail/`, and the card's second measurement run reaches past it. The remaining half is named under "What this does NOT close" below, so the card stays open for it.

Clause-②: no

## The card's attribution is falsified; the symptom is not

The title says the Edit affordance is derived from the object-level `writeScope` only. Measured on `origin/main`:

- **objectui never reads `writeScope`.** `git grep -n writeScope` over `packages/` and `apps/` returns prose comments, plus the metadata-admin permission EDITOR that authors the value. Zero affordance sites read it.
- **All three Edit affordances already AND a record-grained verdict**, and they take it from the authority the card asks for: `POST /api/v1/security/explain` with a `recordId`. The detail header and the drawer go through `plugin-detail`'s `useRecordEditable`; the list row kebab goes through `plugin-grid`'s `useRecordCrudVerdicts`; the console record page imports `useRecordEditable` from this package. The server folds the record share into that verdict (the explain engine's row outcome admits on a `record_share` rule), so the UI is already asking the same question the write path answers.

So the repair the card proposes — "ask the same authority the write path asks" — is already the shipped design. What was wrong is who the answer was remembered FOR.

## What was actually broken

`useRecordEditable` memoises the row verdict in a module-scope `Map`, keyed `object:recordId:operation`. Nothing in that key says which principal the verdict was computed for, and a module-scope map outlives every unmount for the life of the tab.

Signing out does not end that life. This repo already records that no sign-out call site reloads the page — which is exactly why `AuthProvider.signOut` purges the per-tab storage caches by hand (objectui#5198, whose docblock calls the same shape "a cross-principal disclosure, not ordinary staleness"). This map was not among what it purged. Worse, the memo is read by the `useState` INITIALISER, during render: a foreign verdict is adopted synchronously, no probe is ever sent, and no later answer can correct it.

Both fail directions were reachable, and each is now pinned:

| direction | what the previous principal cached | what the next principal gets | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| stale DENY | `false` | `false`, never re-asked | a user holding a record-level `edit` share is shown no Edit for the rest of the tab's life, while `PATCH` on that record succeeds — the shape this card reports |
| stale ALLOW | `true` | `true`, never re-asked | the UI offers Edit to a principal holding no grant — an invitation to a write the server refuses |

The second is the worse one, and it is also the best available explanation for the one control in the card's second run that the reporter could not reproduce: after changing a record's `owner_id` to the test account and re-opening the page in the same tab, Edit still did not appear. The verdict for that `(object, recordId, update)` triple had already been memoised, so the re-test could not have asked again.

## The repair

`packages/plugin-detail/src/useRecordEditable.ts`, three changes, no new permission source and no new published prop:

1. **The key carries the acting principal** — `usePermissions().userId`, the identity `/me/permissions` already publishes (`null` when the client has no answer). The verdict itself still comes from the explain engine alone; this is the identity that verdict belongs to, not a second authority. The key is a `JSON.stringify` of an array rather than a delimited string, so no user id can spell another key by containing the delimiter and "principal unknown" is a value of its own rather than a reserved word.
2. **The map is dropped when that principal changes.** The key alone already makes another principal's entry unreachable, but entries written during a window where the client does not yet know who it is are keyed `null` — and the window between a sign-out and the next sign-in keys to that same `null`. Dropping on change means no entry can span such a change.
3. **A key change with no cached answer resets to the fail-open default** instead of leaving the previous key's verdict on screen across the round trip. That was the same reuse without the map, and it applied to a record or operation change too.

⛔ Unchanged on purpose: the hook's fail-open posture on an unknown answer (ADR-0124 D1 — the server enforces, the client is courtesy), the request shape, the authenticated probe channel, and the memo itself within one principal. `@object-ui/permissions` was already a peer dependency of this package and is already imported by `DetailView` in it, so nothing new is declared.

## Evidence

New pin: `packages/plugin-detail/src/useRecordEditable.principalScope.test.tsx`, four cases — the two cross-principal directions above, plus two that hold the memo itself in place (same principal, and no provider mounted).

Reverse verification, run in both orders on the same tree:

- **Before the source change**, against `origin/main`'s hook: `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. The two failures are exactly the cross-principal pair — "expected true to be false" on the stale-ALLOW pin and the waitFor timeout on the stale-DENY pin. The two memo-preservation cases passed, so the pin is not simply asserting that no cache exists.
- **After**, with the eleven pre-existing pins in `useRecordEditable.test.tsx` alongside: `Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 15 passed (15)`.
- **Ablation, from the committed fix**: restoring only `useRecordEditable.ts` to its base blob turns the same two cases red again and the rest green; restoring from `HEAD` returns the tree to an empty `git diff HEAD`. Both legs and the byte-identity check are in the report on the card.

Gates run locally, each exit code captured to a file before reading: `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check-changeset-presence`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the three touched paths (NOT GOVERNED). Package suite and type-check numbers are in the report on the card.

## What this does NOT close

The card's second measurement run reports that on 17.2.0 the console record page showed no Edit for **every** non-builtin-admin account, including one with `writeScope: 'org'` and including the record's own owner, while `/api/v1/auth/me/permissions`, `/api/v1/security/explain` and `PATCH` all allowed the write. The cache defect fixed here can produce that reading in a single tab that walks account to account, and it explains the failed owner control — but it cannot be shown to be the whole of it from this repo, because the console record page's Edit gate has exactly one other per-user term, and that term is the explain engine's own `record.visible` for `operation: update`, which is computed server-side.

The probe that separates the two, run as the affected account with the page open:

```
POST /api/v1/security/explain   {"object":"kpi_entry_line","operation":"update","recordId":"THE_ID"}
```

Read `record.visible` in the response. If it is `true`, the client-side cache was the whole story and this PR is the fix. If it is `false` while `PATCH` on the same record returns 200, the remaining half is an explain-engine defect and belongs on a platform card, not here — the console is faithfully reflecting a verdict the server got wrong.

## Acceptance notes

Observed while reading, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not touched:

- `plugin-grid`'s `useRecordCrudVerdicts` carries the SAME unkeyed module-scope verdict memo, with the same two fail directions. It is out of this card's file surface and belongs on its own card; noted here so the pair is not repaired one side at a time.
- `MePermissionsProvider.check` looks an object up as `data.objects[object]` with no case normalisation, while its siblings `checkField` and `getObjectApiOperations` both lower-case first and both carry a comment saying the backend stores keys lower-case. A mixed-case `objectName` therefore takes the unknown-object branch, which fails closed for an authenticated session. Not reachable from this card's objects (all lower-case) and not measured against a real payload, so it is an observation, not a finding.
- `packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.optionColors.test.tsx` and `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DatasetWidget.relabel.test.tsx` both cite this hook by a cross-file line address, the form AGENTS.md commandment #11 bans outright. This branch does not falsify either one (the cited line is above every edit and did not move) and `check:new-line-citations` is differential, so it reports 0 new. Carrier: the next change that edits that docblock.
